title: sim-run.test.ts is load-sensitive: tests flake when run beside other files
evidence: Under load (1-min ~7.8), `npx vitest run ios/scripts/` failed 'an old token from a finished run does not skip the lock' (AssertionError: expected +0 to be 75, sim-run.test.ts:221) and, in another run, 'lists the demo device…'; both pass alone (70/70). Timing assumptions: (1) the old-token test (sim-run.test.ts:216-225) starts a holder whose fake command is `sleep 3`, polls until(busy) every 50 ms (10 s cap, :97-99), then expects a second run with HR_SIM_WAIT_SECONDS=1 to give up with 75. It assumes the second run's startup plus its 1 s lockf wait (sim-run.sh:131) ends inside the holder's 3 s; under load it took longer, the holder finished, and the second run took the lock and returned 0. (2) the demo-device test (:563-570) writes demo-booted as now minus 125 s, then expects status to print exactly 'Booted for 2m5s' (sim-run.sh:292 takes the age from the script's own clock). It waits on no fake process; it assumes the status run starts within the same second, so a run slowed past a second boundary prints 2m6s (the exact failing assertion was not captured). Found 2026-11-11 while building lead M17 (PR 1299). Offered to the untangle audit builder, who wrote the load guard (Fable, 2026-11-11). Remedy: give the timing tests generous waits (a longer holder in (1), 2m5s or 2m6s in (2)) or run that file serially (vitest fileParallelism off for it).
